Alex (support): Hi team — ACME (#acct-2871) just escalated. They see streaming responses where TTFB looks fine (~50ms) but p99 total time for the request is huge (8–12s). Non-streaming calls to same model variant are ~200ms p99. Request id: req_20260315_az12. Customer is hitting our hosted API via their on-prem proxy.

Maria (oncall-sre): Thanks, Alex. Can you paste a minimal curl repro and any proxy headers? Also, are they using SSE or HTTP/2 chunked?

Alex (support): Repro from customer (they replaced tenant + keys):

```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \\n  -d '{"model":"rw-llama-13b:2026-03-01","input":"long prompt..."}' \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

They also forwarded a tcpdump showing TCP FIN after long idle before final chunk. Proxy is Nginx 1.22 with default proxy_buffering on.

Jon (runtime): Hmm. Pattern suggests streaming early chunks are flushed (TTFB ok) but finalization or trailing chunks get delayed — likely due to intermediate proxy coalescing or our runtime finalizer waiting to flush last buffer. Can you grab an edge trace? curl --http2 --no-buffer -i -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' should help.

Kevin (CSM): Customer says their UX shows spinner for entire duration even though they see first tokens. They can't tweak their proxy easily. They need a mitigation within our stack if possible.

Maria (oncall-sre): Repro steps I ran against staging: when Nginx proxy_buffering is enabled, we see this behavior if server ends stream with small final packet. Nginx will buffer small writes and flush on buffer or timeout. Behavior differs between http/1.1 chunked vs h2. Example diff:

- client: streaming early chunks -> ok
- Nginx buffers final small chunk -> client waits until buffer_timeout

I can reproduce with:
```bash
# start simple server that writes small final chunk
python -m http.server 8000 &
# curl through nginx with proxy_buffering on/off
```

Jon (runtime): On the runtime side we've got two knobs: `stream_flush.window_ms` (default 40ms) which coalesces tiny writes to reduce syscalls, and `chunk_coalesce.enabled` which merges tokens when under a threshold. For these tenant flows the final token sets may be under the coalesce threshold and get held for window expiry. If their proxy then buffers additionally, p99 spikes.

Sara (product): If we expose header-based hints, client could opt-out but that's not immediate. Could we default disable coalescing for hosted API for tenants behind proxies that opt in? Also need to avoid regressing throughput/cost for normal traffic.

Jon (runtime): Proposed immediate mitigations (fast):
- add per-tenant edge rewrite to set `x-rw-stream-flush=always` which tells runtime to flush final chunks immediately (bypass coalesce).
- add temporary edge rule to set `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for /v1/streams for tenant ACME.

Longer-term: make stream_flush.window_ms adaptive: if downstream shows buffering (we detect ack gaps or small final writes), reduce window for that route.

Maria (oncall-sre): Quick operational fix: create Nginx location rule for this tenant to `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` — Kevin can request their proxy admin to do that. But Kevin said they can't. So edge-side rewrite is better.

Kevin (CSM): I'll ask ACME if they can add the header. They likely can't. Can you add the edge rewrite?

Alex (support): DeployBot shows a small edge config change is possible via our routing console. We can stage a tenant-specific header injection.

DeployBot: edge-change created: echo "add header x-rw-stream-flush: always for tenant acct-2871" | ci pipeline run #3452 — waiting review.

Jon (runtime): While edge change is rolling, here's a quick repro if someone wants to test locally vs ngnix:

1) Run simple node server that streams tokens with final write of 10 bytes
2) Route through nginx with `proxy_buffering on` and default timeouts
3) Observe: first chunks arrive quickly; final bytes delayed by nginx buffer_timeout (default 60s)

Snippet (node):
```js
res.write('data: token1\\n\\n');
setTimeout(() => res.end('data: end\\n\\n'), 1200);
```

Maria (oncall-sre): TL;DR: root cause is multi-hop buffering (runtime coalesce + upstream proxy buffering). P99 blowups happen when finalization path has small tail and both layers hold it. Mitigations: disable coalesce on edge for tenant; add header hints for clients or runtime adaptive mode; fallback to sync endpoint for UX-critical calls.

Sara (product): For product follow-up: add an opt-in header `x-rw-prefer-sync: true` or `x-rw-stream-hint: no-coalesce` so apps can choose sync-like behavior for low-latency UX. Also add doc note about proxies (Nginx, F5) and how they interact.

Jon (runtime): Action items:
- [P0] edge header inject for acct-2871 (Alex/Jon) — ETA 1h (already in review)
- [P1] runtime short-term flag to force final-chunk flush per-tenant — ETA 3d
- [P2] adaptive flush heuristic design doc — ETA 1 week

Alex (support): I'll update ACME with the edge-change and ask them to validate within 30m. Will escalate if they still see >1s p99.

Kevin (CSM): Customer appreciated quick turnaround. They asked for a temporary SLA note while we implement runtime change. I'll coordinate.

Maria (oncall-sre): Also added to incident feed: streaming-p99-multi-hop-buffering — will monitor for other tenants showing same pattern (we can detect TTFB ok + total_time >>).

Jon (runtime): If anyone needs quick test vectors: use `wrk` with HTTP/2 and a long prompt; watch for first-byte vs full response times. Example header we will use for tenant: `x-rw-stream-flush: always` — runtime will honor by bypassing the coalesce window for last write.

Alex (support): Thanks everyone. I'll close this thread once ACME confirms mitigation. :thumbsup:

Kevin (CSM): FYI ACME confirmed reduced spinner time after edge change. P99 dropped to ~300ms. Leaving runtime work in backlog to make this robust.
